# Thesis: Persistent co-movement of volume and VWAP ranks marks crowded trades. (Alpha #50, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term price signals (the recipe that qualified A101_054_acc, IR .137).
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_050 Fast IR .072.
c = ts_corr_binary(cs_rank(volume), cs_rank(vwap_last_hour), 5)  # 5-day corr of volume rank and VWAP rank
r = cs_zscore(-ts_max(cs_rank(c), 5))  # the original signal, z-scored
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996)
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # signal + accruals at 1.5x

# Thesis: A change in where the close sits within the day's range reverts. (Alpha #53, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term price signals (the recipe that qualified A101_054_acc, IR .137).
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_053 Fast IR .068.
pos = ((close - low) - (high - close))/(close - low + 0.001*close)  # close location within the day's range
r = cs_zscore(-delta(pos, 10))  # the original signal, z-scored
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996)
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # signal + accruals at 1.5x

# Thesis: Days when volume growth and the open-to-close return move together tend to reverse. (Alpha #2, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term price signals (the recipe that qualified A101_054_acc, IR .137).
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_002 Fast IR .071.
dv = delta(at_signlog(volume), 2)  # 2-day change in log volume
oc = (close - open)/open  # open-to-close return
r = cs_zscore(-ts_corr_binary(cs_rank(dv), cs_rank(oc), 5))  # the original signal, z-scored
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996)
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # signal + accruals at 1.5x

# Thesis: Persistent high-price/volume co-movement marks crowded moves that fade. (Alpha #15, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term price signals (the recipe that qualified A101_054_acc, IR .137).
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_015 Fast IR .073.
c = ts_corr_binary(cs_rank(high), cs_rank(volume), 3)  # 3-day corr of high-price rank and volume rank
r = cs_zscore(-ts_sum(cs_rank(c), 3))  # the original signal, z-scored
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996)
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # signal + accruals at 1.5x

# Thesis: When volume and high-price both sit at local peaks together, the move is exhausted. (Alpha #26, adapted) Blended with low accruals, whose returns move against short-term price signals (the recipe that qualified A101_054_acc, IR .137).
# Source: Kakushadze, "101 Formulaic Alphas" (2016), https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00991; Sloan, The Accounting Review 1996, https://www.jstor.org/stable/248290
# Repair: accrual partner 1.5x. Parent A101_026 Fast IR .073.
c = ts_corr_binary(ts_rank(volume, 5), ts_rank(high, 5), 5)  # corr of 5-day volume and high ranks
r = cs_zscore(-ts_max(c, 3))  # the original signal, z-scored
k = cs_zscore(-cs_rank((ts_fill(net_income) - ts_fill(cash_from_operations))/ts_fill(total_assets)))  # low accruals: earnings backed by cash (Sloan 1996)
alpha = at_zero2nan(at_nan2zero(r) + 1.5*at_nan2zero(k))  # signal + accruals at 1.5x
